subject: LeapCraft compute safety margin and SLO-fit proposal
messages:
From: Alex Rios <alex.rios@leapcraft.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@leapcraft.ai>
Date: 2026-09-25T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Initial usage profile + SLO questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Samir and I pulled together a short usage profile (attached) and wanted to align on how Redwood would size Dedicated capacity for our production rollout. Key asks:
- We need p95 latency <= 350ms for text generation endpoints (90-token responses typical, some up to 400 tokens in rare long-form cases).
- Average concurrency today ~120 qps, expected to grow to 400 qps over 6 months.
- We’ll route different workloads to different model sizes: a lightweight 7B model for short responses and a 70B variant for long-form.

Can you provide a proposal that maps tokens/sec estimates to GPU counts, plus realistic headroom (safety margin) for traffic bursts and a fallback strategy if we exceed committed capacity?

Appreciate a short sketch we can include with procurement.

Best,
Alex
Co-founder, LeapCraft

Attachments: leapcraft_token_profile.csv, sample_prompts.json

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Alex Rios <alex.rios@leapcraft.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-26T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial usage profile + SLO questions

Alex — thanks for the profile and prompts. I skimmed the CSV; good signal. Ben (SE) and Laura (Solutions) are looped in to run a quick sizing calc and propose options. High level notes from me:

- We’ll map workloads to two serving tiers: short-form (7B, quantized) and long-form (70B, FP16 / quantized depending on quality targets).
- Primary objective: meet p95 <= 350ms while keeping committed GPU footprint as small and predictable as possible.
- Two levers we’ll use: 1) model variant routing by request type, 2) conservative safety margin (we usually recommend 25–40% depending on burstiness).

Ben/Laura — can you produce a short table (tokens/sec -> GPUs) and recommend a committed slab count for LeapCraft with 30% headroom? Also include a fallback plan (hosted overflow + model variant).

I’ll prep a ~1-page proposal for procurement once we have numbers.

— Rishi
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Alex Rios <alex.rios@leapcraft.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.p@leapcraft.ai>
Date: 2026-09-27T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial usage profile + SLO questions

Alex / team — did a quick compute model based on the attached profile and our internal perf numbers. Assumptions first:
- Short-form (7B, int8 quantized): median generation cost ~0.6ms/token on an A100-80GB-equivalent slab with optimized kernels and batching. Effective throughput per GPU ~2,800 tokens/sec under realistic batching (mixed concurrency).
- Long-form (70B, fp16): median generation cost ~3.8ms/token; effective throughput per GPU ~650 tokens/sec. Quantized 70B (4-bit) can push ~1.1x throughput but may degrade some long-form quality depending on prompts.
- Average response length: 90 tokens (short) / 180 tokens (long) for planning; peaks to 400 tokens for <5% of requests.
- Concurrency behavior: your 120->400 qps translates to token/sec at median lengths: 120 qps * mix(70% short / 30% long) * avg_tokens -> ~(120*(0.7*90 + 0.3*180)) = ~16,560 tokens/sec currently; at 400 qps -> ~55,200 tokens/sec.

Sizing table (target p95 <= 350ms):
- Current baseline (120 qps, ~16.5k tokens/sec):
  - Short-form demand: ~8,000 tokens/sec -> need 3 A100-equivalent GPUs (3 * 2,800 = 8,400 tps)
  - Long-form demand: ~8,500 tokens/sec -> need 14 A100-equivalent GPUs (14 * 650 = 9,100 tps)
  - Combined (mixed routing): we recommend separating pools. For Dedicated commitment we size long-form pool and leave short-form on a smaller reserved pool or burst to hosted.
- Growth scenario (400 qps, ~55.2k tokens/sec):
  - Short-form: ~28,000 tokens/sec -> 10 GPUs (10 * 2,800 = 28,000 tps)
  - Long-form: ~27,200 tokens/sec -> 42 GPUs (42 * 650 = 27,300 tps)

Recommendation (commercially practical commit + safety margin):
- Initial dedicated commitment: 20 A100-equivalent GPUs split as: 6 GPUs for short-form pool (handles ~16.8k tps), 14 GPUs for long-form pool (handles ~9.1k tps at current traffic but with headroom for quality FP16).
- This maps to ~30% safety margin on short-form and ~60% on long-form given model inefficiency; we prefer a conservative initial long-form slab because long responses dominate token consumption and tail latency.
- To cover bursts and growth to 400 qps without immediate re-provisioning: enable burst overflow to Redwood hosted for excess long-form requests (automated routing policy) and use quantized 70B variant for non-critical workloads (can give ~10–20% extra throughput).

Operational notes / tradeoffs:
- Latency headroom is tight with long-form on FP16; p95 improvement comes from batching/prefix caching and ensuring KV cache warm-up for long dialogs.
- If LeapCraft requires firm p95 <= 350ms even at peak/400 qps, we recommend a larger initial commitment (30–36 GPUs) or stricter routing to favor smaller models for borderline requests.

Attachments: redwood_proposal_v2.pdf (I’ll drop a one-pager with the table), sample calculation sheet included.

— Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — that table is helpful and the conservative call on long-form makes sense. A few follow-ups before we move to procurement:
- Can you produce a 1-page slide with the conservative (20 GPUs) and aggressive (36 GPUs) commercial scenarios and estimated monthly committed cost ranges? Procurement wants explicit headroom numbers and a clear overflow path (DocuSign-friendly).
- For the quantized 70B suggestion: can we get a quick A/B QA snapshot on a small sample of our prompts so we can understand quality regressions (if any)?
- Could we schedule a 30-min call early next week to run through the proposal with our engineering lead?

I’ll upload the sample prompts to the Drive link you shared. If you can send the one-pager + cost ranges by Monday EOD, we’ll start internal approvals.

Best,
Alex
Co-founder, LeapCraft
